meta.title: Galaxy Space — tonight's sky, made simple
meta.description: Your daily view of the night sky: moon phase, sunrise and sunset, the ISS overhead, and the odds of an aurora tonight.

hero.title: Tonight's sky, without the guesswork
hero.lede: Galaxy Space turns raw space data into one simple daily view: what the moon looks like tonight, when the sun rises and sets, where the ISS is right now, and whether there's a real chance of aurora.

sky.loc_note: Uses your device location if you allow it, or the coordinates you enter. Nothing is stored or sent to a server.
sky.kp_low: Low — unlikely except near the poles

glance.title: Why check tonight?
glance.sub: Four numbers, updated live, that tell you whether it's worth looking up.
glance.card1_body: A new moon means darker skies and better stargazing; a full moon means better moonlit walks.
glance.card2_body: Sunset and sunrise mark your actual dark-sky window, adjusted to your location.
glance.card3_body: The ISS is visible to the naked eye — like a fast, steady star crossing the sky.
glance.card4_body: The Kp-index tells you how likely an aurora is tonight, even far from the poles.

about_page.title: About Galaxy Space
about_page.lede: Why this site exists, and how it works.
about_page.s1_body: Galaxy Space is an independent, one-person project. It pulls a handful of free, public space-data sources into one page, so you can see tonight's sky at a glance instead of hunting across five different apps.
about_page.s2_body: Moon phase is calculated directly in your browser. Sunrise, sunset, and geomagnetic activity come from free public APIs. Nothing about your location is stored on a server — if you share it, it stays in your browser session only.
about_page.s3_body: The Ads page lets readers advertise astrology, tarot, and related services. Every listing is reviewed by a person before it goes live — see the Terms page for details.
about_page.s4_body: Questions, corrections, or partnership ideas are welcome — see the contact details on the Terms page.

terms_page.title: Terms of use
terms_page.lede: Plain-language rules for using Galaxy Space.
terms_page.s1_body: Galaxy Space is provided as-is, free to use, for general informational purposes. Sky data (moon phase, sunrise/sunset, ISS position, geomagnetic activity) is sourced from public data providers and is approximate — it is not a substitute for official aviation, maritime, or scientific data.
terms_page.s2_body: The Ads page allows independent practitioners (astrology, tarot, and related readings) to list their services in exchange for a link back to Galaxy Space. Submitting a listing does not guarantee publication.
terms_page.s3_body: Every submitted listing is reviewed manually before publication. We may reject or remove any listing that is misleading, promises guaranteed outcomes (e.g. medical, legal, or financial guarantees), targets minors, or otherwise violates these terms — without needing to give a reason.
terms_page.s4_body: Galaxy Space does not endorse, verify, or take responsibility for the services listed on the Ads page. Any arrangement you make with an advertiser is between you and them.
terms_page.s5_body: These terms may change as the site evolves. Continued use of the site means you accept the current version.

ads_page.title: Community ads
ads_page.lede: A space for readers to offer astrology, tarot, and related readings — in exchange for linking back here.
ads_page.how_body: Submit your listing through the form below. Every submission is reviewed by a person — never posted automatically — usually within a few days. Once approved, your listing appears here with a link to your site or profile, and we ask that you link back to Galaxy Space in return.
